description:
## What
Implement the per-certificate name constraint enforcement check in chain_walk per RFC 5280 §6.1.4(b)(1)–(2).

## Algorithm
For each cert in the chain (including EE), collect its names:
1. Build name set N:
   - Always include subject DN as DirectoryName
   - If SAN present: include all GeneralName entries from SAN
   - If SAN absent: only the subject DN (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.6)

2. For each name n in N:
   a. EXCLUDED check: if any excluded subtree matches n → return Err(NameConstraintViolation { index })
   b. PERMITTED check: if permitted_subtrees is Some(permitted) AND no permitted subtree matches n →
      return Err(NameConstraintViolation { index })

3. Self-issued intermediates (not the leaf): skip this check (RFC 5280 §6.1.4(b)(1) exception)

## Defensive programming
- Only check name types for which we have constraints (skip unimplemented types silently)
- Run excluded check first (fail fast)
- index = the chain position (0-based) being checked

## Acceptance criteria
- Cert with SAN dNSName=foo.evil.com where .evil.com is excluded → Err(NameConstraintViolation)
- Cert with SAN dNSName=foo.example.com where permitted=[.example.com] → Ok
- Cert with SAN dNSName=foo.other.com where permitted=[.example.com] → Err
- Self-issued intermediate with forbidden name: no error
- Depends on: PKIX-mew (matchers), PKIX-f0m (SAN extractor), PKIX-pjz (error variant)
title: Implement per-cert NC constraint check
